name: Construction Partners, Inc.
reason: Roll-up paving contractor: acquisitions were 4.7x 10y FCF, net debt/EBITDA 3.7x, and EPS 2.21 sits at its 10y max with EBIT margin at a 10y high (9.3% vs 6.0% avg) in a government-funding-dependent cyclical.

name: Roper Technologies, Inc.
reason: High-quality vertical-software compounder (28% EBIT margin, 11.6% 10y EPS CAGR) but growth is acquisition-driven (acq 1.7x 10y FCF, 2.95x net debt/EBITDA, 33% adj-vs-GAAP gap) and its niche application software faces credible AI-disintermediation risk within 5 years.

name: RPM International Incorporated
reason: Good branded coatings/sealants franchise but EPS is 1.0x its 10y max with EBIT margin at a 10y high (12.5%, 100th pctile vs 10.9% avg) on construction-linked demand, and 10% avg ROIC is good-not-special.

name: Red Rock Resorts, Inc.
reason: Las Vegas locals casino operator: discretionary and regional-cycle earnings (EPS -1.28 in 2020, only 2/7 years of 7%+ growth), net debt/EBITDA 4.1x and 3.3% avg ROIC fail the balance-sheet and specialness tests.

name: Reliance, Inc.
reason: Well-run metals service centre but earnings are set by metal prices: EPS 14.26 is 0.47x the 2022 peak of 30.03 and consensus FY3 growth is -10%.

name: Rush Enterprises, Inc.
reason: Commercial truck dealer tied to the Class 8 freight cycle: EPS 2.18 is 0.72x the 2022 peak on a 5.3% EBIT margin; the 10.5% LTM FCF yield partly reflects inventory/floor-plan swings, not a special business.

name: Reliance Worldwide Corp. Ltd.
reason: Plumbing-fittings maker tied to housing repair/remodel with tariff exposure: 5y EPS CAGR -3.3%, EBIT margin 11.9% at the 18th pctile of its history and acquisitions at 1.2x 10y FCF; no clear 7% route.

name: Ryan Specialty Holdings, Inc.
reason: Attractive E&S wholesale-broker franchise, but growth leans on acquisitions (acq 2.0x 10y FCF) and leverage (3.6x net debt/EBITDA), GAAP EPS fell 35% in 2025 with a 167% adj-vs-GAAP gap, and E&S pricing is softening from a cyclical high.

name: Rayonier Inc.
reason: Timber REIT whose earnings follow log and land-sale prices (10y revenue CAGR -1.3%, shares +2.3%/yr) and is mid-merger with PotlatchDeltic; no durable 7% growth route.

name: Safety Insurance Group, Inc.
reason: Massachusetts-concentrated auto/home insurer with 10% avg ROE, 5y EPS CAGR -7.7% (2023 EPS 0.84) and EPS 0.67x its 10y high; disciplined but no growth route or specialness.

name: SBA Communications Corp.
reason: Tower REIT with sticky contracts, but net debt/EBITDA of 8.05x, a three-carrier customer base facing consolidation churn, and FFO/share down 4% in 2025 (12.84 vs 13.37) make the 5-10y path hard to underwrite.

name: Sinclair, Inc.
reason: Local broadcast TV in secular decline with net debt/EBITDA 7.7x, negative GAAP EPS in 4 of the last 6 years and negative consensus EPS; the 14.6% FCF yield is cord-cutting run-off, not a compounder.

name: Service Corporation International
reason: Dominant North American funeral/cemetery network with scale and density advantages, a large preneed backlog and baby-boomer death-rate tailwind; 12.6% 10y EPS CAGR with shares -3.5%/yr, steady ~22% EBIT margin, ~9-10% consensus growth and 3.8x net debt/EBITDA acceptable for a defensive business (FCF is recurring).

name: Stepan Co
reason: Commodity-like surfactants/polyols producer: EPS 1.82 is 0.27x its 2022 high, EBIT margin 3.0% at the 9th pctile and FCF yield only 1.8% after a heavy capex cycle.

name: SEI Investments Company
reason: Debt-free (net cash) platform with 27.5% avg ROIC, but fees are largely asset-based so earnings track market levels, and EPS is 1.0x its 10y max with consensus LTG only 2.5%.

name: Septerna, Inc.
reason: Clinical-stage GPCR biotech with no product revenue and losses (EPS -1.10); positive FCF came from one-off partnership upfront payments, so outcomes are binary.

name: Somnigroup International Inc.
reason: Tempur Sealy just transformed itself by acquiring Mattress Firm: net debt/EBITDA 5.25x is too high for a discretionary, housing-linked durable, and the integration makes the record a poor guide.

name: Sotera Health Company
reason: Essential sterilisation/lab-testing oligopoly with a 35.8% EBIT margin, but ethylene-oxide tort litigation and EPA EO rules are a credible 5-year threat, alongside 3.5x net debt/EBITDA and a 257% adj-vs-GAAP gap.

name: Sunstone Hotel Investors, Inc.
reason: Upper-upscale hotel REIT with cyclical RevPAR-driven earnings: FFO 0.86 is still below 2015's 1.31, avg ROIC is 2.1%, and there is no specialness.

name: Steven Madden, Ltd.
reason: Fashion footwear wholesaler with China-sourcing tariff exposure and a leveraged Kurt Geiger acquisition: EPS 1.70 is 0.61x its 2022 high with EBIT margin at the 18th pctile; fashion risk makes it unforecastable.
